## Freshman Champions Over the Past 10 Years

Winning an NCAA Division I wrestling national championship as a true freshman or redshirt freshman is an exceptional feat. The chart below tracks every year from 2015 through 2026, showing the number of true and redshirt freshmen who stood atop the NCAA podium.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

freshman_champs <- tribble(
  ~year, ~wrestler, ~school, ~weight, ~type,
  2015, "Nathan Tomasello", "Ohio State", "125 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2015, "Isaiah Martinez", "Illinois", "157 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2016, "Myles Martin", "Ohio State", "174 lb", "True Freshman",
  2017, "Mark Hall", "Penn State", "174 lb", "True Freshman",
  2017, "Vincenzo Joseph", "Penn State", "165 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2017, "Bo Nickal", "Penn State", "184 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2018, "Spencer Lee", "Iowa", "125 lb", "True Freshman",
  2018, "Yianni Diakomihalis", "Cornell", "141 lb", "True Freshman",
  2019, "Mekhi Lewis", "Virginia Tech", "165 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2021, "AJ Ferrari", "Oklahoma State", "197 lb", "True Freshman",
  2021, "David Carr", "Iowa State", "157 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2021, "Carter Starocci", "Penn State", "174 lb", "Redshirt Freshman",
  2021, "Aaron Brooks", "Penn State", "184 lb", "Redshirt Freshman"
)

yearly_champs <- tibble(year = 2015:2026) |>
  left_join(
    freshman_champs |>
      group_by(year) |>
      summarise(
        total = n(),
        details = paste(
          paste0("• ", wrestler, " (", school, ", ", weight, " — ", type, ")"),
          collapse = "<br>"
        ),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "year"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    total = replace_na(total, 0),
    details = case_when(
      !is.na(details) ~ details,
      year == 2020 ~ "Tournament canceled due to COVID-19",
      year == 2026 ~ "Upcoming championship / 0 to date",
      TRUE ~ "No freshman champions"
    )
  )

plot_ly(
  data = yearly_champs,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~total,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  marker = list(size = 10, color = "#2c7fb8"),
  line = list(color = "#2c7fb8", width = 2.5),
  text = ~details,
  hovertemplate = paste(
    "<b>Year: %{x}</b><br>",
    "Freshman Champions: %{y}<br><br>",
    "%{text}<extra></extra>"
  )
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(text = "NCAA DI True & Redshirt Freshman Champions (2015–2026)"),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Year",
      dtick = 1,
      range = c(2014.5, 2026.5)
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Number of Champions",
      dtick = 1,
      rangemode = "tozero"
    )
  )
```

This graph itself shows that over time in the past three years there have been an increasing number of NCAA champs that are either true freshmans or redshirt freshmans. Meaning that the level of competition is getting higher and so does the skill along with it. This is happening mainly due to the reason that wrestling as a sport is becoming more popular so more kid programs are being made so there are kids going into college with around 15 years of wrestling under their belt. The graph fails to show that the freshman and each generation is just getting better, improving along with the sport, and that more experience might not be the factor for getting wins but being younger and hungrier for a win. So this chart is a sort of promise I made to myself that if true freshmen are able to be a national champ at the division 1 level then I am surely able to make it to an all american level within the NAIA as a freshman just getting ready to improve.
